chunks: Muʿāwiyah ibn ʿAmmār narrated from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام that he said:

There is no ihram except after a prescribed prayer or a recommended prayer. If it is a prescribed prayer, you enter ihram after it, after the taslim. If it is a recommended prayer, you pray two rakʿahs and enter ihram after it. Then when you finish the prayer, praise Allah, Mighty and Majestic, extol Him, send blessings upon the Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, and say:

O Allah, I ask You to make me among those who respond to You, believe in Your promise, and follow Your command. For I am Your servant and in Your grasp; I am not protected except by what You protect, and I take nothing except what You give. You have mentioned hajj, so I ask You to determine it for me according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet صلى الله عليه وآله, strengthen me in what I am weak concerning, receive my rites from me in ease and well-being from You, and make me among Your delegation whom You have been pleased with, chosen, named, and written down. O Allah, I have come out from a distant land and spent my wealth seeking Your pleasure. O Allah, complete my hajj for me. O Allah, I intend tamattuʿ.

according to Your Book and the sunnah of Your Prophet, Your blessings be upon him and his family. If some obstacle arises for me and restrains me, then release me where You have restrained me, by Your decree which You have decreed upon me. O Allah, if it is not a hajj, then an ʿumrah. My hair, skin, flesh, blood, bones, marrow, and nerves enter ihram for You, from women, clothes, and perfume, seeking thereby Your Face and the Hereafter.
It suffices you to say this once when you enter ihram. Then stand and walk a little, and when the ground becomes level with you, whether you are walking or riding, then recite the talbiyah.

key_terms.إِحْرَامٌ: the consecrated state entered for hajj or ʿumrah
key_terms.التَّسْلِيمِ: the concluding salutation ending the prayer
key_terms.التَّمَتُّعَ: the form of hajj combining ʿumrah before hajj
key_terms.الْحَجَّ: the pilgrimage rite being intended and requested from Allah
key_terms.مَنَاسِكِي: my pilgrimage rites and ritual acts

ai.seo_question: How should one enter ihram according to the hadith of Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the proper time and manner of entering ihram, linking it to prayer and a specific supplication. It combines legal instruction for hajj rites with a du'a expressing servitude, reliance upon Allah, intention for tamattuʿ, and conditional release if prevented.
